result.title: Detection and Validation of Hidden Subgroup Disparities in Clinical AI
result.summary: Machine learning (ML) models used in clinical workflows often perform systematically differently across patient groups, raising concerns about equity and patient safety. Traditional subgroup analyses can expose such disparities only when rich metadata (e.g., patient demographics) is available and captures the sources of performance variation, conditions rarely met in practice. Algorithmic subgroup discovery methods offer a solution by identifying coherent groups from learned feature representations, but because true underlying stratifications are unknown, these methods are hard to evaluate. As a result, subgroup discovery has not been systematically applied or assessed for performance monitoring. Our main objective is to evaluate algorithmic subgroup discovery for performance monitoring, assessing the discovered subgroups' performance gaps and semantic coherence. Investigating cardiomegaly classification in a dataset of 223,228 chest X-rays, we showed that the discovered subgroups exhibited larger performance gaps (accuracies of 0.61-0.90) than traditional metadata-based analysis (0.80-0.94) and were frequently interpretable using patient, acquisition, and model metadata. As a proof of concept, we also showed that annotations from learned subgroups can be used to mitigate the biases they expose. We conclude that subgroup discovery is a practical and effective tool to enhance the performance validation and monitoring of ML systems in healthcare.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作在 22 万余张胸片的心脏增大分类任务上评估「算法式子群发现」用于性能监测：从学习到的特征表示中聚类出语义连贯的患者子群，其准确率跨度为 0.61–0.90，差距大于基于元数据的分组分析，并初步用子群标注缓解已暴露的偏差。
AI.relevance_reason: 从内部特征表示中发现并验证隐藏子群的做法，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态聚类与失败归因、以及判断视觉细节与任务必要信息是否保留在表示中，但其本身不研究推理过程或 latent 生成。
